Checking the leg model

I want to be able to trace a motor command back to the geometry that produced it.

I started with geometric IK in Python, then developed analytical C++ kinematics and a separate derivation using transforms. That work meant checking signs, frames, and derivatives carefully, while keeping mathematical checks separate from tests on the robot.

FK, IK & Jacobian: the derivation history ↗Python → C++: what changed in the controller ↗Browse original handwritten PDFs ↗

From sketches to a Jacobian

The connection between position and velocity
p = f(q)
vfoot = J(q)q̇
J(q) = ∂f / ∂q

The Jacobian comes from differentiating the leg model. Its signs depend on how I define the joint angles and leg frame, and its units depend on the lengths used in that model.

Body orientation and feedback

I studied how torso orientation error can become a foot correction and then a joint command. My notes work through geometric posture correction, quaternion and axis-angle error, and foot motion in a rotating body frame.

A velocity expressed in a rotating frame
vfoot,world = vbody,world + R(vfoot,body + ωbody × rfoot,body)

Here, ω and r use body-frame coordinates, and R rotates the result into the world frame. The equation describes kinematics; whole-body dynamics control needs its own validation.

The saved numerical results

In the saved October 18, 2026 MATLAB study, I checked the same leg model using homogeneous transforms, symbolic differentiation, geometric Jacobian columns, and numerical perturbations.

6,000sampled configurations
9.65 × 10−11maximum Jacobian discrepancy against finite differences · m/rad
1.76 × 10−16maximum IK position round-trip error · m

These are saved offline results for the recorded model and source snapshot; the study was not rerun for this website update. Some controller files have since changed. The figures measure agreement between the numerical models; physical tracking needs separate tests.

CAD mass and inertia

I checked the exported components, center of mass, inertia orientation, and coordinate frames before using the CAD model for dynamics. A model can look complete while leaving hardware out of its mass calculation.

An earlier corrected simulation snapshot has 13 links, 12 moving joints, and 12.54 kg of CAD-derived mass. That mass belongs to this CAD component snapshot; physical robot revisions need separate weight measurements.

Rotate and shift each component inertia
Itotal = Σ [RiIiRiᵀ + mi((di·di)I − didiᵀ)]

Each inertia tensor is rotated into the same frame and shifted to the overall center of mass using the parallel-axis theorem. The model uses the listed component masses without global scaling.

verify_mass_correction.py · inertia aggregationPython / NumPy
axes = b.ximat[index].reshape(3, 3)
delta = b.xipos[index] - center
inertia += axes @ np.diag(new.body_inertia[index]) @ axes.T
inertia += new.body_mass[index] * (
    np.dot(delta, delta) * np.eye(3) - np.outer(delta, delta)
)

Further control and learning work

My independent study covers PD system behavior, state estimation, LQR, centroidal MPC, and PPO. I want to test whether a learned correction can improve a conventional controller whose behavior I understand. I have not yet demonstrated that hybrid approach.

Current stage

The model and training pipeline are a starting point.

The short policy runs check that the pipeline works. Learned walking and trotting, reliable terrain traversal, and transfer to the real robot still need to be demonstrated. My LQR and MPC work remains study and preliminary formulation.
